# Section 5: Troubleshooting — Refrigeration Systems (Continued)

## 5.7 Evaporator Fan Motor Replacement (Models NW-18, NW-21, NW-24)

The evaporator fan motor is located behind the rear panel inside the freezer compartment. On model NW-24, the motor is mounted on a slide-out bracket; on NW-18 and NW-21, it is secured with two screws to the evaporator housing.

**Tools required:** 5/16" nut driver, flat-blade screwdriver, needle-nose pliers.

**Procedure:**

1. Disconnect power to the unit.
2. Remove all food from the freezer compartment. Place food in a cooler or another freezer.
3. Remove the rear panel by pulling the bottom edge outward and lifting up. The panel is held by two tabs at the top.
4. Disconnect the fan motor wiring harness. The connector is a two-pin Molex type; press the locking tab and pull straight out.
5. Remove the fan blade by holding the motor shaft with pliers and turning the blade counterclockwise. The blade is a press-fit; do not pry against the blade fins.
6. Remove the motor mounting screws.
7. Install the new motor. Reattach the fan blade, pushing it on until it seats against the motor shoulder.
8. Reconnect the wiring harness. Route the wires so they do not contact the fan blade.
9. Reinstall the rear panel. Ensure the tabs are fully seated before pressing the panel into place.
10. Restore power. The fan should start within 30 seconds of the compressor starting.

**Torque specification:** Motor mounting screws, 12 in-lb. Do not overtighten; the motor housing is aluminum and will strip.

**Note:** On units manufactured after March 2022, the fan motor connector is a four-pin type. The extra two pins are for a tachometer signal. If you are replacing a motor on a post-March 2022 unit, use the NW-24 motor kit (part no. 821-447) which includes the tachometer harness. The older two-pin motor will not provide a tach signal and will cause the board to log a fan fault after 10 minutes of runtime.

## 5.8 Condenser Fan Motor Replacement (Models NW-18, NW-21, NW-24)

The condenser fan motor is mounted under the unit, behind the kickplate. On NW-18 and NW-21, the motor is mounted to a bracket that also holds the condenser coil. On NW-24, the motor is mounted directly to the compressor deck.

**Procedure:**

1. Disconnect power.
2. Remove the kickplate (two screws, one at each end).
3. Disconnect the motor wiring. The connector is located near the compressor; follow the wire harness from the motor.
4. Remove the fan blade. The blade is held by a spring clip; compress the clip with pliers and slide the blade off the shaft.
5. Remove the motor mounting bolts (three bolts, 1/4" hex head).
6. Install the new motor. Reattach the fan blade, ensuring the concave side faces the condenser coil.
7. Reconnect the wiring.
8. Reinstall the kickplate.
9. Restore power. Check that the fan rotates freely and does not rub against the shroud.

**Airflow direction:** The condenser fan pulls air through the condenser coil from the rear of the unit and discharges it out the front. If the fan blade is installed backwards, the unit will overheat and the compressor will cycle on the overload protector.

## 5.9 Defrost Heater Replacement (Models NW-18, NW-21, NW-24)

The defrost heater is a glass-tube type, located under the evaporator coil. It is held in place by two clips at each end.

**Procedure:**

1. Disconnect power.
2. Remove the rear panel inside the freezer compartment (see Section 5.7, steps 1–3).
3. Disconnect the heater wiring. The heater has two leads with spade connectors; note the position of each lead before disconnecting.
4. Remove the heater from the clips. The heater may be frozen to the evaporator; use a heat gun on low setting to loosen it. Do not use a torch.
5. Install the new heater. Ensure the heater is centered under the evaporator and the leads are routed through the strain relief.
6. Reconnect the wiring. The heater leads are not polarized; either lead can go to either terminal.
7. Reinstall the rear panel.
8. Restore power.

This manual is organized into the following sections:

Section 1 – General Information and Safety
Section 2 – Common Tools, Fasteners, and Torque Specifications
Section 3 – Diagnostic Flowcharts and Fault Codes
Section 4 – Refrigeration Systems (Residential)
Section 5 – Refrigeration Systems (Light Commercial)
Section 6 – Laundry Appliances (Washers and Dryers)
Section 7 – Cooking Appliances (Ranges, Ovens, Cooktops)
Section 8 – Dishwashers and Disposers
Section 9 – Electrical Systems and Control Boards
Section 10 – Parts Replacement Tables and Interchangeability

Sections 4, 5, 7, and 10 contain the largest number of changes and should be reviewed in full before performing any maintenance in those areas. Section 2 includes updated torque specifications for all fastener classes used in current production. These values supersede those in MM-2023, and the Engineering Change Notice (ECN) numbers are listed in the revision history for traceability.

1.1 Scope and Application

This manual applies to all Northwind appliances bearing a model number starting with the following prefixes: NR (residential refrigeration), NC (light commercial refrigeration), NW (washers), ND (dryers), NK (ranges and ovens), NH (cooktops), and NQ (dishwashers and disposers). Units manufactured before 2017 may require procedures from the legacy manual set; where a difference exists, the legacy manual takes precedence for those older units, and the difference is noted in the applicable section. Units manufactured from 2017 through 2023 are covered by this manual unless a specific bulletin states otherwise.

The procedures in this manual are written for technicians who have completed the Northwind factory training program or hold an equivalent certification accepted by the Service Division. Some procedures require the use of specialized tools that are listed in Section 2.3. Do not substitute tools unless the substitute is explicitly approved in the text. In all cases, follow local, state, and federal safety regulations, including lockout/tagout procedures where applicable.

Maintenance Manual MM-2024 supersedes Maintenance Manual MM-2023. Record status: superseded.

1.5 Torque Specifications

Torque values in this manual are given in inch-pounds (in-lb) unless otherwise noted. Values are for dry threads unless the procedure specifies lubricant. If a fastener is removed and reinstalled, always apply the torque value listed in the current revision, not the value that was used at the factory. Factory torque values may have been updated by an engineering change.

| Fastener Location | Size | Torque (in-lb) | Rev |
|-------------------|------|----------------|-----|
| Compressor mounting bolts | 5/16 in. | 120 ± 10 | B |
| Compressor discharge line nut | 7/16 in. | 180 ± 15 | B |
| Oven door hinge bolts (upper) | M8 | 95 ± 5 | C |
| Oven door hinge bolts (lower) | M8 | 95 ± 5 | C |
| Oven door inner glass retainer | M5 | 25 ± 3 | C |
| Control board mounting standoffs | M3 | 8 ± 1 | D |
| Evaporator fan blade nut | 1/4 in. | 35 ± 5 | A |

Revision C changed the oven door hinge bolt torque from 85 in-lb to 95 in-lb. The change was made to address intermittent hinge loosening reported in the field. Do not use the MM-2023 value of 85 in-lb. If you encounter a unit with hinge bolts that were torqued to the old specification, retorque them to the new value during any service visit that involves the oven door.
